entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alcetas I of Macedon was the king of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedon, a member of the Argead dynasty and son of Aeropus I.




 Alcetas I ruled Macedon during a period of significant cultural and political transformation, as the region was increasingly influenced by the Persian Empire and the rise of the city-state of Athens.







 His reign saw the development of the Macedonian army, which would later become a key factor in the conquests of Philip II and Alexander the Great.







 Alcetas I's legacy extends beyond his own kingdom, as his policies and military tactics influenced the development of Hellenistic kingdoms in the region.
